logic.note: I2C at 0x68 with the register map, auto-incrementing pointer and wrap-around: BCD seconds to year with century bit, 12/24-hour mode, the time latched at START for consistent multi-byte reads, the oscillator-stop flag (cleared by writing 0), control/aging registers, and the temperature registers in 0.25 °C steps.

timing.note: The clock runs with simulation time, exactly (0 ppm). Writing the time restarts the second like the chip's countdown chain. Alarms are stored but never fire.

analog.note: Temperature is whatever the temperature prop says, rounded to 0.25 °C; on the chip it is measured every 64 s.

power.note: Fixed 0.2 mA from VCC; answers I2C only above 2.3 V. The backup battery is not modelled: the time survives power loss and lostPower is a prop.

emulates: Registers 0x00-0x12 with BCD time and date, century bit and 12/24-hour mode
Time copied to the read buffer at START, so RTClib's 7-byte read never tears
Setting the time (rtc.adjust) and the oscillator-stop flag (rtc.lostPower)
Temperature registers (rtc.getTemperature) from the temperature prop
Deterministic start time from the startTime prop
doesNotEmulate: Alarm matching, the A1F/A2F flags and the SQW/INT interrupt output
Crystal drift, aging offset and temperature compensation
The AT24C32 EEPROM at 0x57 that many ZS-042 modules carry
The day-of-week register as written: it is always derived from the date
testOnRealDevice: Drift over days (about 2 ppm, one minute a year)
Keeping time on the coin cell with the board unpowered; some ZS-042 modules charge the cell and damage non-rechargeable CR2032s
